summary: Sequoia National Park lookout tower in use by 1929 and staffed into 1944; register dates a first structure to 1934 and a 1966 replacement. Removal date unknown.

facts.design: 1934 observation-only cabin on a 40 ft X-brace steel tower with a residence cabin; 1966 CL-100 plan 13x13 cabin on a steel K-brace tower
facts.status_note: Register lists removal as Unknown and gives no removal date for the 1966 structure; no source describes the site now

events.note: Newspaper notices show the Ash Peak lookout station open to visitors by August 1929; a 1932 notice speaks of the tower's completion in 1929. The register's first-structure date is 1934.
J. G. Wade had charge of the tower for three seasons as of September 1930; earliest named keeper in our sources
Homer Cooper, Wade's brother-in-law, took up the summer station at the tower
George Magley was fire lookout at Ash Peak for the 1933 season

Register: first structure, an observation-only cabin on a 40 ft X-brace steel tower, with a residence cabin. April 1934 notices still have Magley in charge at the Ash Peak tower, with a new tower planned at Little Baldy.
Paul Ortlipp was to have charge for the 1938 fire season; the Ash Peak station was used again instead of the newer Little Baldy station
Charles Miller was to take his post at the Ash Peak lookout; latest named keeper in our sources
Register: the structure was replaced by a CL-100 plan 13x13 cabin on a steel K-brace tower

corrections.proposed: 1934 first structure per register; 1966 is the replacement CL-100 cabin on a steel K-brace tower
corrections.why: The register dates the first structure to 1934 and gives 1966 for the replacement, and newspaper notices show a lookout in use before 1966.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1934 for the first structure. Newspaper notices show an Ash Peak lookout tower in use by 1929, and a 1932 notice gives 1929 as its completion. Both dates are kept in the story.

sources.title: Ash Peak (Mountain) - FOREST LOOKOUTS
sources.publisher: Forest Lookouts (California), quoting period newspaper notices

notes_for_editor: Brief's built 1966 is the replacement year, not the first structure. The 1929 newspaper dates and the register's 1934 start disagree; both are kept. No source describes what remains on the site today, and the register does not say whether the summit is open to visitors. The brief's status 'gone' is not supported: the register lists removal as Unknown, so status is set to unknown. A 1966 National Park Service photo of the Ash Peak lookout structures exists in the NPS NPGallery (public domain, photographer Richard McLaren) but no direct image URL was confirmed, so it is not added to photos.
